claim: The X-chromosome gene regulatory process called dosage compensation ensures that males (1X) and females (2X) express equal levels of X-chromosome transcripts.
source_text: The X-chromosome gene regulatory process called dosage compensation ensures that males (1X) and females (2X) express equal levels of X-chromosome transcripts.
evidence_reasoning: This is a well-established concept in genetics and represents established scientific knowledge about dosage compensation.

claim: Approximately 70% of C. elegans genes undergo a rapid co-transcriptional processing event in which the 5′ end is replaced by a common 22-nucleotide leader RNA (SL1) through a trans-splicing mechanism.
source_text: Nascent RNA transcripts from approximately 70% of C. elegans genes undergo a rapid co-transcriptional processing event in which the 5′ end is replaced by a common 22-nucleotide leader RNA (SL1) through a trans-splicing mechanism
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Blumenthal, 2012, indicating prior published work established this finding.

claim: C. elegans equalizes X-chromosome expression between the sexes by reducing Pol II recruitment to promoters of hermaphrodite X-linked genes using a chromosome-restructuring condensin complex.
source_text: We find that C. elegans equalizes X-chromosome expression between the sexes, to a level equivalent to autosomes, by reducing Pol II recruitment to promoters of hermaphrodite X-linked genes using a chromosome-restructuring condensin complex.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding of the manuscript supported by GRO-seq and GRO-cap experimental data comparing wild-type and dosage-compensation-defective animals, combined with inference from the data patterns.

claim: The DCC binds to both X chromosomes of hermaphrodites to reduce transcription by half.
source_text: The DCC binds to both X chromosomes of hermaphrodites to reduce transcription by half
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to Meyer, 2010 and Pferdehirt et al., 2011, indicating prior published work.

claim: The DCC shares subunits with condensin, a protein complex required for the compaction, resolution, and segregation of mitotic and meiotic chromosomes.
source_text: The DCC shares subunits with condensin (Csankovszki et al., 2009; Mets and Meyer, 2009), a protein complex required for the compaction, resolution, and segregation of mitotic and meiotic chromosomes (Wood et al., 2010)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by multiple citations indicating prior published work established these relationships.

claim: GRO-seq experiments from three stages of wild-type animals (embryos, starved L1 larvae, and L3 larvae) and dosage-compensation-defective embryos had high statistical correlation between biological replicates (Spearman correlation, ρ > 0.94).
source_text: The two GRO-seq biological replicates for each stage had high statistical correlation throughout the genome (Spearman correlation, ρ > 0.94)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by statistical analysis of the experimental GRO-seq data from biological replicates.

claim: A TSS was identified for 31.7% (6353 genes) of all C. elegans protein-coding genes from at least one of the three developmental stages examined.
source_text: In total, a TSS was identified for 31.7% (6353 genes) of all C. elegans protein-coding genes from at least one of the three developmental stages examined
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result directly derived from the GRO-cap and GRO-seq experimental data analysis.

claim: Of TSS calls, 77% are for genes shown previously to be trans-spliced.
source_text: Of our TSS calls, 77% are for genes shown previously to be trans-spliced
evidence_reasoning: This claim combines data from the current study with prior published work (Allen et al., 2011) on trans-splicing.

claim: Outrons can be as long as 14 kb and have a median of 260 bp and mean of 753 bp.
source_text: We found instead that outrons can be as long as 14 kb and have a median of 260 bp and mean of 753 bp
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding directly derived from analysis of the TSS and trans-splice acceptor site data.

claim: 59% of outrons are longer than 200 bp, 21% are longer than 1 kb, and 2.3% are longer than 5 kb.
source_text: Fully 59% of outrons are longer than 200 bp, 21% are longer than 1 kb, and 2.3% are longer than 5 kb
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result directly derived from analysis of outron length distributions in the experimental data.

claim: Many trans-spliced genes have multiple TSSs.
source_text: Many trans-spliced genes have multiple TSSs (Figure 3A), suggesting that trans-splicing has removed the selective pressure to form promoters with a single TSS.
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation from the GRO-cap data with an inferred evolutionary explanation.

claim: Trans-splicing has removed the selective pressure to form promoters with a single TSS.
source_text: suggesting that trans-splicing has removed the selective pressure to form promoters with a single TSS
evidence_reasoning: This is an evolutionary inference drawn from the observation that trans-spliced genes have multiple TSSs.

claim: Genes can use different TSSs across developmental stages, indicating developmental stage-specific regulation of transcription initiation.
source_text: Genes can use different TSSs across developmental stages, indicating developmental stage-specific regulation of transcription initiation
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation from comparing GRO-cap data across developmental stages with an inference about regulatory mechanisms.

claim: DNA sequences flanking the newly annotated TSSs have strong sequence conservation across nematode species.
source_text: DNA sequences flanking the newly annotated TSSs have strong sequence conservation across nematode species
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by phastCons conservation analysis across seven Caenorhabditis species as shown in the supplementary data.

claim: DNA sequences flanking newly annotated TSSs have evolutionarily conserved core promoter elements, including the TATA-box (worm consensus TATAWAWR) and the initiator element (Inr) (worm consensus YCAYTY).
source_text: DNA sequences flanking the newly annotated TSSs have evolutionarily conserved core promoter elements, including the TATA-box (worm consensus TATAWAWR)...and the initiator element (Inr) (worm consensus YCAYTY)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by MEME motif search analysis of sequences surrounding the experimentally determined TSSs.

claim: Of 4547 embryo genes with TSSs, 162 genes (3.6%) have a TATA element with a perfect match to the consensus 15–45 bp upstream of it.
source_text: Of 4547 embryo genes with TSSs, 162 genes (3.6%) have a TATA element with a perfect match to the consensus 15–45 bp upstream of it
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from motif search analysis of the TSS data.

claim: 745 genes (16.4%) have an Inr with the adenine residing at the TSS (+1 bp).
source_text: 745 genes (16.4%) have an Inr with the adenine residing at the TSS (+1 bp)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from motif search analysis of the TSS data.

claim: Accumulation of Pol II at 3′ ends of genes is abundant in C. elegans.
source_text: Accumulation of Pol II at 3′ ends of genes is abundant
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed in the GRO-seq data showing elevated signal at 3′ ends of genes.

claim: 3′ End pausing is more extensive in C. elegans than in Drosophila.
source_text: A histogram of the 3′ end pausing ratios shows 3′ accumulation of Pol II is more extensive in Caenorhabditis elegans than in Drosophila.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by comparative analysis of 3′ pausing ratios calculated from GRO-seq data in C. elegans and Drosophila.

claim: Genes at the beginning and middle of operons had higher 3′ accumulation than genes at the end of operons or not in operons.
source_text: Genes at the beginning (n = 430) and middle (n = 276) of operons were more highly expressed and had higher 3′ accumulation than genes at the end (n = 474) of operons or not in operons (n = 5048).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from analysis of GRO-seq signal at 3′ ends of genes in different operon positions.

claim: Pol II 3′ accumulation is positively correlated with the expression level of the gene in C. elegans.
source_text: Pol II 3′ accumulation, likely caused by slow 3′ end formation and RNA processing (Gromak et al., 2006), is positively correlated in C. elegans with the expression level of the gene
evidence_reasoning: This correlation is demonstrated in the GRO-seq data (Spearman correlation of 0.776), with mechanistic interpretation supported by citation.

claim: 3′ Pol II accumulation is likely caused by slow 3′ end formation and RNA processing.
source_text: Pol II 3′ accumulation, likely caused by slow 3′ end formation and RNA processing (Gromak et al., 2006)
evidence_reasoning: This mechanistic explanation is supported by citation to prior work and is consistent with the observed data patterns.

claim: Upstream divergent transcription is common at promoters of C. elegans genes.
source_text: Upstream divergent transcription is common at promoters of C. elegans genes.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed in the GRO-seq data showing antisense transcription upstream of TSSs.

claim: Divergent transcripts are short and initiated 75–150 bp upstream from TSSs of promoters lacking upstream divergent genes.
source_text: In C. elegans, divergent transcripts are short and initiated 75–150 bp upstream from TSSs of promoters lacking upstream divergent genes
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from analysis of GRO-seq and GRO-cap data at promoters.

claim: The frequency of upstream divergent transcription in C. elegans appears to be intermediate in degree between that in mammals and that in Drosophila.
source_text: The frequency of upstream divergent transcription in C. elegans appears to be intermediate in degree between that in mammals, where it occurs at the majority of active promoters (Kapranov et al., 2007; Core et al., 2008; Seila et al., 2008), and that in Drosophila, where it occurs only rarely (Nechaev et al., 2010; Core et al., 2012)
evidence_reasoning: This comparative claim is supported by analysis of the current GRO-seq data and comparison with published data from other organisms.

claim: For both mammals and worms, promoters with TATA elements rarely support divergent transcription.
source_text: For both mammals and worms, promoters with TATA elements rarely support divergent transcription
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by analysis of the current data and comparison with published mammalian data (Core et al., 2012).

claim: Expression of her-1 was elevated 12.7-fold in sdc-2 mutants.
source_text: her-1 was de-repressed 12.7-fold
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from comparing GRO-seq signal between sdc-2 mutant and control embryos.

claim: The increase in GRO-seq signal for her-1 was uniform from the promoter to the 3′ end, suggesting that SDC-2 controls sex determination by reducing Pol II recruitment or initiation at the her-1 promoter in XX embryos.
source_text: the increase in GRO-seq signal was uniform from the promoter to the 3′ end, suggesting that SDC-2 controls sex determination by reducing Pol II recruitment or initiation at the her-1 promoter in XX embryos
evidence_reasoning: The uniform increase is observed in the data, and the mechanistic interpretation is inferred from this pattern.

claim: The median change of gene expression in sdc-2 mutant vs control embryos was an increase of 1.63- to 1.67-fold for X-linked genes of all lengths.
source_text: The median change of gene expression in sdc-2 mutant vs control embryos was an increase of 1.63- to 1.67-fold for X-linked genes of all lengths
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from statistical analysis of GRO-seq data comparing mutant and control embryos.

claim: The median change of gene expression in sdc-2 mutant vs control embryos was a slight reduction of 0.79- to 0.81-fold for autosome-linked genes.
source_text: The median change of gene expression in sdc-2 mutant vs control embryos was...a slight reduction of 0.79- to 0.81-fold for autosome-linked genes
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from statistical analysis of GRO-seq data comparing mutant and control embryos.

claim: For the subset of X and autosomal genes whose expression was statistically different (p≤0.05) between mutant and control embryos, 99% of X-linked genes had elevated expression in the mutants.
source_text: For the subset of X and autosomal genes whose expression was statistically different (p≤0.05) between mutant and control embryos, 99% of X-linked genes had elevated expression in the mutants
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from statistical analysis (DESeq) of GRO-seq data.

claim: 63–66% of autosomal genes with statistically different expression had reduced expression in sdc-2 mutants.
source_text: 63–66% of autosomal genes had reduced expression
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from statistical analysis of GRO-seq data comparing mutant and control embryos.

claim: Most embryonically expressed X-linked microRNAs are dosage compensated.
source_text: We found most embryonically expressed X-linked microRNAs to be dosage compensated
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by analysis of GRO-seq signal for microRNA genes in sdc-2 mutant vs control embryos.

claim: X-linked tRNAs are not dosage compensated, implying that RNA polymerase II is broadly sensitive to dosage compensation, and RNA polymerase III is insensitive.
source_text: while X-linked tRNAs were not, implying that RNA polymerase II is broadly sensitive to dosage compensation, and RNA polymerase III is insensitive
evidence_reasoning: The lack of dosage compensation for tRNAs is observed in the data, and the mechanistic interpretation about polymerase specificity is inferred.

claim: The peak of DCC binding is immediately upstream of the TSS.
source_text: Mapping of new TSSs relative to DCC binding sites called from our ChIP-seq experiments performed for this comparison showed the peak of DCC binding to be immediately upstream of the TSS.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct result from comparing ChIP-seq data for DCC subunit DPY-27 with the newly mapped TSSs.

claim: DCC binding to a gene is neither necessary nor sufficient for the compensation of that gene.
source_text: Although the DCC binds to promoter regions, prior studies showed that DCC binding to a gene is neither necessary nor sufficient for the compensation of that gene, and not all genes are dosage compensated (Jans et al., 2009).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by prior published work and confirmed by the current analysis comparing DCC binding with gene expression changes.

claim: The DCC can act at a distance to control gene expression.
source_text: Thus, the DCC can act at a distance to control gene expression
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation that DCC binding intensity does not correlate with the degree of dosage compensation at individual genes.

claim: DCC binding intensity is not a proxy for the dosage compensation status of the gene.
source_text: and DCC binding intensity is not a proxy for the dosage compensation status of the gene
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by analysis showing no correlation between DPY-27 ChIP-seq signal and expression changes in sdc-2 mutants.

claim: Promoter-proximal pausing of transcriptionally engaged Pol II is a rate-limiting step of transcription in metazoans.
source_text: Promoter-proximal pausing of transcriptionally engaged Pol II is a rate-limiting step of transcription in metazoans
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations to Adelman and Lis, 2012 and other references.

claim: Promoter-proximal pausing is rare in C. elegans embryos.
source_text: we found promoter-proximal pausing to be rare in C. elegans embryos
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed in the GRO-seq data, with only 15 of 3975 genes showing 5′ pausing in wild-type embryos.

claim: In starved L1s, 7.7% of genes (166 of 2133) exhibit 5′ pausing, and most were on autosomes.
source_text: In starved L1s, we found 7.7% of genes (166 of 2133) to exhibit 5′ pausing, and most were on autosomes
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from analysis of GRO-seq data in starved L1 larvae.

claim: Genes not paused in embryos can become paused in L1s deprived of food.
source_text: genes not paused in embryos become paused in L1s deprived of food
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by comparing GRO-seq profiles of specific genes across developmental stages.

claim: Pol II pausing can be induced by food deprivation.
source_text: Our results confirm their proposal that Pol II pausing can be induced by food deprivation.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the current GRO-seq data and confirms a prior proposal by Baugh et al., 2009.

claim: C. elegans appears to lack NELF, which contributes to pausing in other organisms.
source_text: C. elegans appears to lack NELF, which contributes, in part, to pausing in other organisms (Yamaguchi et al., 1999)
evidence_reasoning: This is based on genome annotation knowledge and supported by citation about NELF function.

claim: 5′ pausing control is highly implausible as the mechanism of X-chromosome dosage compensation in embryos.
source_text: These cumulative results make it highly implausible that 5′ pausing control is the mechanism of X-chromosome dosage compensation in embryos
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from the rarity of 5′ pausing in embryos and the lack of enrichment on X chromosomes.

claim: Analysis of GRO-seq data revealed a uniform increase in the level of engaged Pol II across the entire length of X-linked genes, from TSSs to 3′ ends, in sdc-2 mutants.
source_text: Analysis of GRO-seq data comparing transcriptionally engaged Pol II in control vs dosage-compensation-defective XX embryos revealed a uniform increase in the level of engaged Pol II across the entire length of X-linked genes, from TSSs to 3′ ends, in the sdc-2 mutants
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed in metagene analysis and heat maps of GRO-seq data comparing mutant and control embryos.

claim: The ratio of engaged polymerase in sdc-2 mutant vs control was consistently elevated by at least 1.6-fold across scaled X-linked genes, from TSSs to 3′ ends.
source_text: For the metagene analysis, the ratio of engaged polymerase in mutant vs control was consistently elevated by at least 1.6-fold across scaled X-linked genes, from TSSs to 3′ ends
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from metagene analysis of GRO-seq data.

claim: Metagene analysis of autosomal genes showed only a slight decrease in engaged Pol II across their lengths in sdc-2 mutants.
source_text: In contrast, metagene analysis of autosomal genes from the same data sets showed only a slight decrease in engaged Pol II across their lengths
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed in metagene analysis of GRO-seq data for autosomal genes.

claim: The dosage compensation mechanism reduces X-linked gene expression in C. elegans hermaphrodites by restricting either the recruitment or initiation of Pol II.
source_text: these results demonstrate that the dosage compensation mechanism reduces X-linked gene expression in C. elegans hermaphrodites by restricting either the recruitment or initiation of Pol II
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from the uniform increase in Pol II across gene lengths in mutants, as observed in GRO-seq data.

claim: Dosage compensation does not preferentially affect Pol II elongation.
source_text: The ratios of indices between control and mutant embryos were not significantly different for genes on X compared to autosomes, indicating that dosage compensation does not preferentially affect Pol II elongation
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by analysis of elongation density indices showing no significant difference between X and autosomal genes.

claim: Re-analysis of genome-wide ChIP-chip analysis of Pol II binding relative to the new TSSs showed an approximately twofold increase in the occupancy of hypo-phosphorylated Pol II at the promoters of X-linked genes in sdc-2 mutant vs control embryos.
source_text: re-analysis of our previous genome-wide ChIP-chip analysis of Pol II binding (Pferdehirt et al., 2011) relative to the new TSSs showed an approximately twofold increase in the occupancy of hypo-phosphorylated Pol II at the promoters of X-linked genes in sdc-2 mutant vs control embryos
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from re-analyzing published ChIP-chip data using the newly mapped TSSs.

claim: DNA-bound hypo-phosphorylated Pol II at promoters is enriched for non-initiated Pol II.
source_text: DNA-bound hypo-phosphorylated Pol II at promoters is enriched for non-initiated Pol II
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about the phosphorylation state of Pol II at different stages of transcription.

claim: Pol II promoter recruitment is rate-limiting when dosage compensation is active.
source_text: The increase in Pol II occupancy at promoters of mutants (measured by ChIP) was nearly equivalent to the increase in post-initiated Pol II (measured by GRO-seq), indicating that Pol II promoter recruitment is rate limiting when dosage compensation is active.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from comparing the magnitude of increases in ChIP and GRO-seq signals in mutants.

claim: In sdc-2 mutants, the levels of sense and upstream divergent transcription were elevated coordinately at promoters on X lacking upstream divergent genes.
source_text: in sdc-2 mutants, the levels of sense and upstream divergent transcription were elevated coordinately at promoters on X lacking upstream divergent genes
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed by analyzing sense and antisense GRO-seq signal at promoters in mutant vs control embryos.

claim: At promoters lacking upstream divergent genes, the level of hypo-phosphorylated Pol II was elevated about twofold in sdc-2 mutant vs control embryos.
source_text: At those promoters, the level of hypo-phosphorylated Pol II was also elevated about twofold in mutant vs control embryos, as assayed by ChIP
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from ChIP-chip analysis of Pol II occupancy at specific promoters.

claim: C. elegans dosage compensation controls X-chromosome-wide gene expression predominantly by reducing Pol II recruitment to promoters of hermaphrodites.
source_text: Our combined experiments demonstrate that C. elegans dosage compensation controls X-chromosome-wide gene expression predominantly by reducing Pol II recruitment to promoters of hermaphrodites.
evidence_reasoning: This is the primary conclusion of the study, supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence including GRO-seq, ChIP, and analysis of divergent transcription.

claim: C. elegans has a mechanism to equalize expression between X chromosomes and autosomes.
source_text: Caenorhabditis elegans has a mechanism to equalize expression between X chromosomes and autosomes.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by metagene analysis showing the X to autosome expression ratio is 0.9 in control embryos.

claim: In dosage-compensation-defective mutants, the level of X-chromosome expression exceeds that of autosomes by 1.7-fold.
source_text: In dosage-compensation-defective mutants, the level of X-chromosome expression exceeds that of autosomes by 1.7-fold.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from metagene analysis comparing X and autosomal gene expression in sdc-2 mutants.

claim: A separate regulatory mechanism functions in C. elegans to elevate the intrinsic level of transcription from the X chromosomes of both sexes.
source_text: We also show that a separate regulatory mechanism functions in C. elegans to elevate the intrinsic level of transcription from the X chromosomes of both sexes, so that after dosage compensation, X chromosomes and the two sets of autosomes have equivalent expression.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation that X expression equals autosomal expression in wild-type but exceeds it in mutants, implying an X-upregulation mechanism.

claim: GRO-cap has advantages over TSS mapping strategies that use total accumulated RNA or short-capped (sc) RNA as the starting material.
source_text: GRO-cap has advantages over TSS mapping strategies that use total accumulated RNA or short-capped (sc) RNA as the starting material.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the methodological design and comparison with other approaches.

claim: The use of nascent RNAs without base hydrolysis or size selection enriches the proportion of 5′ capped RNAs within the starting RNA population.
source_text: The use of nascent RNAs without base hydrolysis or size selection, as in GRO-cap, enriches the proportion of 5′ capped RNAs within the starting RNA population
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference about the methodological approach based on the properties of nascent RNAs.

claim: GRO-cap reduces the level of false TSS calls from RNAs that are capped post-transcriptionally.
source_text: reduces the level of false TSS calls from RNAs that are capped post-transcriptionally (Fejes-Toth et al., 2009)
evidence_reasoning: This advantage is inferred from the method design and supported by citation about post-transcriptional capping.

claim: GRO-cap increases the probability of identifying TSSs from promoters that are transcribed at low levels.
source_text: and increases the probability of identifying TSSs from promoters that are transcribed at low levels
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference about the sensitivity advantage of the GRO-cap method.

claim: The GRO-cap strategy permits reliable assignment of TSSs by pairing TSS calls with uninterrupted GRO-seq signal for transcriptionally engaged Pol II between the GRO-cap TSS and the previously annotated 5′ end.
source_text: Most importantly, the GRO-cap strategy permits reliable assignment of TSSs by pairing TSS calls with uninterrupted GRO-seq signal for transcriptionally engaged Pol II between the GRO-cap TSS and the previously annotated 5′ end.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about the methodological advantage of combining GRO-cap with GRO-seq data.

claim: Multiple lines of evidence showed that GRO-cap signal combined with continuous GRO-seq signal from WB starts defines true TSSs.
source_text: Multiple lines of evidence showed that GRO-cap signal combined with continuous GRO-seq signal from WB starts defines true TSSs.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple validation approaches including comparison with ChIP data, lack of 3′ UTRs in outrons, and conservation analysis.

claim: From 565 outrons >1 kb in length, only 1.4% had an identified 3′ UTR.
source_text: From 565 such outrons, only 1.4% had an identified 3′ UTR
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from analyzing 3′ UTR annotations in long outron regions.

claim: The TSSs for the 21 U-RNAs were 2 bp upstream from the mature RNA.
source_text: The TSSs for the 21 U-RNAs were 2 bp upstream from the mature RNA
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from GRO-cap analysis of 21 U-RNA genes showing 4783 (91%) of TSSs were precisely 2 bp upstream.

claim: Of 9148 mature, non-overlapping 21 U-RNAs, 5260 (57.5%) had a putative TSS with a GRO-cap Z-score greater than 3.
source_text: Of these RNAs, 5260 (57.5%) had a putative TSS with a GRO-cap Z-score greater than 3 in the 10 bp interval (p<0.01).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from statistical analysis of GRO-cap signal at 21 U-RNA loci.

claim: 21 U-RNAs receive a 5′ cap and are processed to the mature sequence by removing the two 5′-most base pairs.
source_text: indicating that 21 U-RNAs receive a 5′ cap and are processed to the mature sequence by removing the two 5′-most base pairs
evidence_reasoning: This processing mechanism is inferred from the consistent 2 bp offset between TSSs and mature RNA starts.

claim: Condensin II in Drosophila induces axial compaction of interphase chromosomes, globally disrupts inter-chromosomal interactions, and promotes dispersal of peri-centric heterochromatin.
source_text: Condensin II in Drosophila induces axial compaction of interphase chromosomes, globally disrupts inter-chromosomal interactions, and promotes dispersal of peri-centric heterochromatin (Bauer et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This claim about condensin function is supported by citation to prior published work.

claim: Nematodes carrying mutations that disrupt condensin I display elongated chromosomal axes during meiotic prophase and exhibit chromosome-wide changes in the distribution of double strand breaks and crossovers.
source_text: Furthermore, nematodes carrying mutations that disrupt condensin I, which shares four subunits with the DCC, display elongated chromosomal axes during meiotic prophase and exhibit chromosome-wide changes in the distribution of double strand breaks and crossovers (Mets and Meyer, 2009)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to prior published work on condensin I mutants.

claim: Chromosome compaction and associated topological changes in DNA could broadly affect promoter accessibility of Pol II and the regulatory factors that recruit or stabilize it.
source_text: Chromosome compaction and associated topological changes in DNA could broadly affect promoter accessibility of Pol II and the regulatory factors that recruit or stabilize it, thereby reducing Pol II recruitment in a quantitatively similar manner at different sites.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative model for how condensin might affect Pol II recruitment based on known condensin activities.

claim: Compaction of interphase chromosomal territories could reduce the local concentration of bound transcription activators and hence bound Pol II.
source_text: Compaction of interphase chromosomal territories could reduce the local concentration of bound transcription activators and hence bound Pol II.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative model for how chromosome structure changes might affect transcription.

claim: Changes in intra-chromosomal interactions could alter the relationships between distal regulatory regions and their target promoters, thereby limiting Pol II recruitment.
source_text: Changes in intra-chromosomal interactions could alter the relationships between distal regulatory regions and their target promoters, thereby limiting Pol II recruitment.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative model for how condensin-mediated structural changes might affect gene regulation.

claim: In Drosophila melanogaster, dosage compensation is achieved by the male-specific lethal (MSL) complex that binds along the single X chromosome of males to double transcription of X-linked genes.
source_text: In Drosophila melanogaster, dosage compensation is achieved by the male-specific lethal (MSL) complex that binds along the single X chromosome of males to double transcription of X-linked genes
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about Drosophila dosage compensation supported by citations.

claim: The MSL complex contains two long non-coding RNAs and five proteins, including the H4K16 histone acetyltransferase MOF and the H2BK34 ubiquitin ligase MSL2.
source_text: The complex contains two long non-coding RNAs and five proteins, including the H4K16 histone acetyltransferase MOF (Hilfiker et al., 1997; Conrad et al., 2012a) and the H2BK34 ubiquitin ligase MSL2 (Wu et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This claim about MSL complex composition is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: The MSL complex was proposed to regulate gene expression by controlling transcription elongation.
source_text: The MSL complex was proposed to regulate gene expression by controlling transcription elongation (Smith et al., 2001).
evidence_reasoning: This is a prior model supported by citation to Smith et al., 2001.

claim: The elongation model for fly dosage compensation received support from genome-wide mapping of MSL proteins and MSL-dependent H4K16ac to the bodies of male X-linked genes, with a bias toward 3′ ends.
source_text: This model was subsequently supported by genome-wide mapping of MSL proteins and MSL-dependent H4K16ac to the bodies of male X-linked genes, with a bias toward 3′ ends (Alekseyenko et al., 2006; Gilfillan et al., 2006; Legube et al., 2006)
evidence_reasoning: This supporting evidence is from prior published ChIP studies cited in the text.

claim: GRO-seq experiments in S2 cells with or without RNAi of the msl2 gene supported the elongation model for fly dosage compensation.
source_text: and GRO-seq experiments in S2 cells with or without RNAi of the msl2 gene (Larschan et al., 2011)
evidence_reasoning: This supporting evidence is from a prior published GRO-seq study.

claim: The elongation model for fly dosage compensation received further support from the discovery that dosage compensation is disrupted by impairing the function of SPT5, a transcription elongation factor that co-localizes with the MSL complex on male X chromosomes.
source_text: The elongation model received recent further support from the discovery that dosage compensation is disrupted by impairing the function of SPT5, a transcription elongation factor that co-localizes with the MSL complex on male X chromosomes and interacts physically with the MSL complex (Prabhakaran and Kelley, 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This supporting evidence is from a prior published study on SPT5 function.

claim: The weight of evidence strongly favors enhancement of transcription elongation as the primary mechanism of fly dosage compensation.
source_text: Thus, the weight of evidence strongly favors enhancement of transcription elongation as the primary mechanism of fly dosage compensation.
evidence_reasoning: This is a synthesis and interpretation of multiple lines of published evidence about Drosophila dosage compensation.

claim: In worms, reduction in X-chromosome gene expression is primarily achieved by reducing recruitment of Pol II to promoters, while in flies, elevation in X-chromosome gene expression is primarily achieved by facilitating Pol II transcription elongation.
source_text: In worms, reduction in X-chromosome gene expression is primarily achieved by reducing recruitment of Pol II to promoters, while in flies, elevation in X-chromosome gene expression is primarily achieved by facilitating Pol II transcription elongation.
evidence_reasoning: This comparative conclusion combines the current study's findings with published work on Drosophila.

claim: Multiple solutions have evolved to coordinately control gene expression across an entire chromosome.
source_text: Multiple solutions have evolved to coordinately control gene expression across an entire chromosome.
evidence_reasoning: This is an evolutionary inference drawn from the observation of different mechanisms in worms and flies.

claim: The evolution of sex chromosomes resulted in males having one X chromosome and females having two.
source_text: In many species, the evolution of sex chromosomes to be the primary determinants of sexual fate resulted in males having one X chromosome and females having two.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about sex chromosome evolution in many species.

claim: Such chromosome sex-determining mechanisms had the potential to cause two problems in gene expression: an imbalance in X-chromosome gene expression between the sexes and an imbalance in gene expression between the male X chromosome and his two sets of autosomes.
source_text: Such chromosome sex-determining mechanisms had the potential to cause two problems in gene expression, an imbalance in X-chromosome gene expression between the sexes and an imbalance in gene expression between the male X chromosome and his two sets of autosomes
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference about the consequences of sex chromosome evolution based on gene dosage principles.

claim: X-chromosome dosage compensation strategies such as the Drosophila strategy solved both problems by doubling transcription of the single male X chromosome.
source_text: X-chromosome dosage compensation strategies such as the Drosophila strategy solved both problems by doubling transcription of the single male X chromosome.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about Drosophila dosage compensation supported by the literature.

claim: Nematodes and mammals evolved a strategy to co-evolve two mechanisms: one to increase expression of X chromosomes in both sexes, and a second to decrease total expression from female X chromosomes.
source_text: An alternative solution would be to co-evolve two mechanisms, one to increase expression of X chromosomes in both sexes, thereby preventing hypo X expression in males, and a second to decrease total expression from female X chromosomes to prevent hyper X expression relative to female autosomes and male X chromosomes. Nematodes and mammals evolved the second strategy for equalizing X-chromosome expression between the sexes.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about evolutionary strategies based on known dosage compensation mechanisms in different organisms.

claim: The bulk of evidence now favors the presence of a mechanism to up-regulate X-chromosome expression in males and females of both nematodes and mammals.
source_text: The bulk of evidence now favors the presence of a mechanism to up-regulate X-chromosome expression in males and females of both organisms (Deng et al., 2011, 2013; Jue et al., 2013)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to recent published studies on X upregulation.

claim: The current study provides the most compelling evidence to date for X upregulation in C. elegans.
source_text: and our results provide the most compelling evidence to date for C. elegans
evidence_reasoning: This is a claim about the significance of the current study's findings relative to prior work.

claim: Examining nascent transcripts in mixed-stage embryos by GRO-seq enabled quantification of transcription specifically from somatic embryonic cells and avoided contamination from maternally contributed germline transcripts.
source_text: Our approach of examining nascent transcripts in mixed-stage embryos by GRO-seq conferred three advantages. First, it enabled us to quantify transcription specifically from somatic embryonic cells and thereby avert the complication of quantifying maternally contributed germline transcripts that contaminate mature embryo mRNA.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about the methodological advantage of using nascent transcripts rather than mature mRNA.

claim: GRO-seq examination of nascent transcripts allowed analysis at a stage for which most germline-specific mechanisms of gene regulation would have been erased.
source_text: Second, we could examine nascent transcription at a stage for which most germline-specific mechanisms of gene regulation would have been erased.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about the developmental timing advantage of the experimental approach.

claim: GRO-seq could quantify transcriptionally engaged Pol II across the entire length of a gene, starting from the bona fide TSS.
source_text: Third, we could quantify transcriptionally engaged Pol II across the entire length of a gene, starting from the bona fide TSS
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about the technical advantage of the GRO-seq method combined with accurate TSS mapping.

claim: A major part of the mechanism to increase X expression in C. elegans is to increase the level of Pol II recruitment to promoters.
source_text: We found that a major part of the mechanism to increase X expression in C. elegans is to increase the level of Pol II recruitment to promoters, as was shown recently for mammals (Deng et al., 2013).
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from the GRO-seq data showing X expression equals autosomal expression, and is compared with similar findings in mammals.
